paragraphs.source_en: If one were to write down everything that happens in twenty-four hours from beginning to end, and then read it all through from beginning to end, it would take at least twenty-four hours, would it not? Though I am an ardent advocate of sketch-from-life writing, I must frankly confess that this is, after all, not an accomplishment within the reach of us cats. For that reason, although my master produces by day any number of strange sayings and strange acts well worth recording in detail, it is a great pity that I have neither the ability nor the patience to report each one of them to my readers. Regrettable though it is, there is simply no help for it. Even we cats, after all, require rest. After Suzuki and Meitei had gone, the biting winter wind suddenly ceased, and all around became as still as a night when fine snow falls softly and steadily. My master, as usual, withdrew again into his study. The children of the house lay asleep side by side in the six-mat room. Beyond the nine-foot sliding partition, in the south-facing room, my master's wife had also lain down and was nursing Menko, not yet three years old. In the flower-clouded third month of spring, the day had hastened to dusk and the sun had long since gone down; even the sound of wooden clogs passing along the street could be heard distinctly in the sitting room. From a nearby lodging house came the sound of a Ming flute, breaking off and starting again, now and then giving my drowsy eardrums a dull irritation. Outside, it was probably a dim, hazy night. Dinner had been soup with boiled fish-cake; having licked clean the portion allotted to me in my abalone shell and filled my belly, I could not possibly do without rest.

units.source_en: If one were to write down everything that happens in twenty-four hours from beginning to end, and then read it all through from beginning to end, it would take at least twenty-four hours, would it not?
units.source_zh: 一天二十四小时发生的事，如果都从头到尾写下来，再从头到尾读上一遍，那么至少也要花上二十四小时吧。

paragraphs.source_en: I have heard faint rumors that in this world there is a haikai-flavored phenomenon called the mating cries of cats, and that in early spring nights we feline folk cannot sleep quietly in the alleys but wander about; I, however, have not yet encountered any such change of heart. To be sure, love is the vital force of the universe. From Jupiter, god in heaven, down to the earthworms and mole crickets chirping underground, all things lose themselves in this way; thus it is only natural that even we cats should feel a dim excitement and develop a dangerous taste for romance liable to bring endless trouble. Looking back, I myself, who say this, once pined desperately for Miss Tortoiseshell. Even Miss Tomiko, the daughter of Kaneda, the champion of triangular doctrine and a young lady fond of holding forth on Abekawa rice cakes, is said to have been in love with Kangetsu. For that reason, I have not the slightest intention of scorning all the tomcats and she-cats under heaven for not sleeping through a spring night worth a thousand pieces of gold, but roaming about in distraction, as if they were merely courting vexation and burning with desire. Yet if, though tempted, no such desire arises in me, what am I to do? In my present condition, I desire only rest. When one is this sleepy, love is quite impossible. I slowly made my way to the edge of the children's bedding and lay down to sleep in perfect comfort...

units.source_en: I have heard faint rumors that in this world there is a haikai-flavored phenomenon called the mating cries of cats, and that in early spring nights we feline folk cannot sleep quietly in the alleys but wander about; I, however, have not yet encountered any such change of heart.
units.source_zh: 据我耳闻，世上有所谓猫恋叫春这种俳谐趣味的现象，据说我们这些猫族们每当早春时节夜晚在巷内就无法安寝，到处游荡，但是在下却还没有碰到过这样的心理变化。

units.source_en: To be sure, love is the vital force of the universe.
units.source_zh: 说起来恋爱本是宇宙间的活力。

units.source_en: From Jupiter, god in heaven, down to the earthworms and mole crickets chirping underground, all things lose themselves in this way; thus it is only natural that even we cats should feel a dim excitement and develop a dangerous taste for romance liable to bring endless trouble.
units.source_zh: 上至天神朱庇特，下至在土中鸣叫的蚯蚓、蝼蛄，所有的万物无不为此道而神魂颠倒，因此即使我们这些猫儿也朦胧地感到兴奋，自然而然地产生了会招致许多麻烦的风流念头。

units.source_en: Looking back, I myself, who say this, once pined desperately for Miss Tortoiseshell.
units.source_zh: 回想起来，说这话的在下，也曾对三毛姑娘倾慕得要死呢。

units.source_en: Even Miss Tomiko, the daughter of Kaneda, the champion of triangular doctrine and a young lady fond of holding forth on Abekawa rice cakes, is said to have been in love with Kangetsu.
units.source_zh: 就连主张“三角主义”的金田君的千金——喜欢大谈阿部川饼的富子小姐，据说也爱慕过寒月君哪。

units.source_en: For that reason, I have not the slightest intention of scorning all the tomcats and she-cats under heaven for not sleeping through a spring night worth a thousand pieces of gold, but roaming about in distraction, as if they were merely courting vexation and burning with desire.
units.source_zh: 正因为如此，在下决不认为那满天下的雄猫牝猫不趁着千金一刻的春宵去睡大觉而到处乱转，是什么自找烦恼欲火中烧而加以轻蔑。

units.source_en: Yet if, though tempted, no such desire arises in me, what am I to do?
units.source_zh: 但在下虽受诱惑却产生不了那样的欲念，这又有什么办法呢？

units.source_en: In my present condition, I desire only rest.
units.source_zh: 以在下目前的状态而言，我只是希望休息。

units.source_en: When one is this sleepy, love is quite impossible.
units.source_zh: 困到如此地步，当然无法去恋爱啦。

units.source_en: I slowly made my way to the edge of the children's bedding and lay down to sleep in perfect comfort...
units.source_zh: 我慢条斯理地找到小孩们的被角处，美滋滋地倒头便睡……

paragraphs.source_zh: 据我耳闻，世上有所谓猫恋叫春这种俳谐趣味的现象，据说我们这些猫族们每当早春时节夜晚在巷内就无法安寝，到处游荡，但是在下却还没有碰到过这样的心理变化。说起来恋爱本是宇宙间的活力。上至天神朱庇特，下至在土中鸣叫的蚯蚓、蝼蛄，所有的万物无不为此道而神魂颠倒，因此即使我们这些猫儿也朦胧地感到兴奋，自然而然地产生了会招致许多麻烦的风流念头。回想起来，说这话的在下，也曾对三毛姑娘倾慕得要死呢。就连主张“三角主义”的金田君的千金——喜欢大谈阿部川饼的富子小姐，据说也爱慕过寒月君哪。正因为如此，在下决不认为那满天下的雄猫牝猫不趁着千金一刻的春宵去睡大觉而到处乱转，是什么自找烦恼欲火中烧而加以轻蔑。但在下虽受诱惑却产生不了那样的欲念，这又有什么办法呢？以在下目前的状态而言，我只是希望休息。困到如此地步，当然无法去恋爱啦。我慢条斯理地找到小孩们的被角处，美滋滋地倒头便睡……

paragraphs.source_en: I suddenly woke and opened my eyes, and there was my master, who at some point had come from the study into the bedroom and slipped under the quilt laid beside his wife. It is my master's habit whenever he goes to bed to bring a small foreign-language book from the study, but once he lies down he has never read as much as two pages of it. Sometimes he even brings the book and places it by his pillow, then falls asleep without so much as touching it. If he sometimes does not read even a single line, one would think there is no need to bring it at all; yet this is precisely what makes my master my master, and no matter how his wife laughs at him or tells him to stop, he will not listen. Every night, with prodigious pains, he still carries into the bedroom a book he is not going to read. At times he grows greedy and brings three or four volumes at once. For a while the other day, he even carried Webster's great dictionary in every night. I think this is a kind of illness in my master: just as luxurious people cannot fall asleep unless they hear the pine-breeze sound made by a fine Ryubundo iron kettle, so my master cannot sleep unless he has books beside his pillow. Reasoning from this, for my master books are not things to be read, but instruments for inducing sleep; one might call them printed sleeping medicine.

units.source_en: I suddenly woke and opened my eyes, and there was my master, who at some point had come from the study into the bedroom and slipped under the quilt laid beside his wife.
units.source_zh: 我突然醒来，睁眼一看，我家主人不知什么时候从书斋来到卧室已钻进铺在他妻子旁边的被窝里。

units.source_en: It is my master's habit whenever he goes to bed to bring a small foreign-language book from the study, but once he lies down he has never read as much as two pages of it.
units.source_zh: 主人的毛病是每次睡觉都一定要从书斋里拿来一小本外文书，但是他躺下后从来没有读上过两页。

units.source_en: Sometimes he even brings the book and places it by his pillow, then falls asleep without so much as touching it.
units.source_zh: 有时甚至将书拿来放在枕旁，连摸都没有摸就睡着了。

units.source_en: If he sometimes does not read even a single line, one would think there is no need to bring it at all; yet this is precisely what makes my master my master, and no matter how his wife laughs at him or tells him to stop, he will not listen.

units.source_en: I think this is a kind of illness in my master: just as luxurious people cannot fall asleep unless they hear the pine-breeze sound made by a fine Ryubundo iron kettle, so my master cannot sleep unless he has books beside his pillow.
units.source_zh: 我想这是主人的一种病，正像那些摆阔气的人如果听不到龙文堂精制的铁釜所发出的松涛声就不能安睡一样，主人也是不把书放在枕旁就不能入睡的吧。

units.source_en: Reasoning from this, for my master books are not things to be read, but instruments for inducing sleep; one might call them printed sleeping medicine.
units.source_zh: 由此推理下去，对主人来说，书不是供人读的，而是催眠之物，也可以说是印刷的安眠药吧。

paragraphs.source_zh: 我突然醒来，睁眼一看，我家主人不知什么时候从书斋来到卧室已钻进铺在他妻子旁边的被窝里。主人的毛病是每次睡觉都一定要从书斋里拿来一小本外文书，但是他躺下后从来没有读上过两页。有时甚至将书拿来放在枕旁，连摸都没有摸就睡着了。既然有时连一行都不去读，似乎满可以不必拿来，而这正是主人的特点，不管主人的妻子怎样嘲笑他，劝他不要拿来，可他就是不听。每天晚上还是不厌其烦把书拿到卧室里来。有时他还贪心不足，一次就抱来三四本。前些日子他每晚甚至把《韦氏大辞典》也抱来了。我想这是主人的一种病，正像那些摆阔气的人如果听不到龙文堂精制的铁釜所发出的松涛声就不能安睡一样，主人也是不把书放在枕旁就不能入睡的吧。由此推理下去，对主人来说，书不是供人读的，而是催眠之物，也可以说是印刷的安眠药吧。

paragraphs.source_en: I wondered whether my master had brought something tonight as well. When I looked, a thin little red book lay half open in a position where it nearly blocked the tips of my master's mustache. Judging from the fact that the thumb of his left hand was still caught between the pages, it seemed that, most unusually, he had read five or six lines tonight. Beside the red book lay the usual nickel-plated pocket watch, giving off a chill color quite unsuited to the mild spring night.

units.source_en: I wondered whether my master had brought something tonight as well.
units.source_zh: 我想，今晚主人也会拿来什么书吧？

units.source_en: When I looked, a thin little red book lay half open in a position where it nearly blocked the tips of my master's mustache.
units.source_zh: 一瞧，一册薄薄的小红书在几乎要堵住主人嘴上胡子的地方半开着。

units.source_en: Judging from the fact that the thumb of his left hand was still caught between the pages, it seemed that, most unusually, he had read five or six lines tonight.

units.source_en: Beside the red book lay the usual nickel-plated pocket watch, giving off a chill color quite unsuited to the mild spring night.
units.source_zh: 和那本红书并排放着的是那块镀镍的怀表，发着与和暖的春夜不相称的寒色。

paragraphs.source_zh: 我想，今晚主人也会拿来什么书吧？一瞧，一册薄薄的小红书在几乎要堵住主人嘴上胡子的地方半开着。从主人左手大拇指还夹在书中来看，真是十分难得，他好像已读了五六行。和那本红书并排放着的是那块镀镍的怀表，发着与和暖的春夜不相称的寒色。
